healthInsurance.title: Health Insurance
healthInsurance.heroSubtitle: Protect yourself and your loved ones with health insurance. Find the perfect plan for your needs.
healthInsurance.coverageBenefit: BENEFIT FROM COMPREHENSIVE HEALTH INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR YOUR PEACE OF MIND
healthInsurance.allAboutHealthInsuranceContent: When living in Switzerland, you are required to take out health insurance (LAMal). This covers a portion of your healthcare costs. How does LAMal work? How much does it cost? Do I also need to take out supplementary insurance (LCA)? What are the specific features of health coverage for cross-border commuters? Discover everything you need to know about health insurance in Switzerland.
healthInsurance.whatToKnow: Health insurance in Switzerland: what you need to know
healthInsurance.whatToKnowContent: In 1996, a federal law made membership of LAMal mandatory. In other words, anyone living in Switzerland is obliged to take out this health insurance.
healthInsurance.howItWorks: How does health insurance in Switzerland work?
healthInsurance.howItWorksContent: The objective of Swiss health insurance is to guarantee access to basic healthcare in the event of illness, maternity, or accident. However, it is neither centralised nor government-run. It is the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH) that controls how private insurers administer health protection as part of their activity.
healthInsurance.basicInsurancePoint1: Covers the policyholder's main health needs
healthInsurance.basicInsurancePoint2: Guarantees at least hospitalisation costs in a shared room
healthInsurance.basicInsurancePoint3: Dental costs and alternative medicine, among others, are not covered by mandatory basic health insurance (LAMal)
healthInsurance.chooseInsurer: You are free to choose the health insurer with whom you wish to take out a health insurance contract. All family members must be insured, including children.
healthInsurance.newResidents: New Swiss residents have 3 months to choose their health insurer. After this period, the cantonal administration automatically assigns them a provider.
healthInsurance.premiumsVary: Health insurance premiums for 2024 vary depending on:
healthInsurance.sameReimbursement: Regardless of these factors, the reimbursement level is the same for everyone.
healthInsurance.subsidies: However, it is possible to benefit from reductions on mandatory health insurance premiums, called subsidies. These aids, paid by the canton, can cover all or part of the premiums.
healthInsurance.howToGet: How to obtain mandatory health insurance?
healthInsurance.freeToChoose: All policyholders are free to choose the provider with whom they wish to take out a health insurance contract. The insurer does not have the right to refuse an application. They are also not allowed to ask a prospective policyholder to complete a health questionnaire when signing the contract.
healthInsurance.compareFactors: As each insurer can set the premium they wish, it is important to compare several proposals, taking into account:
healthInsurance.compareFactor1: The budget available for mandatory health insurance
healthInsurance.compareFactor4: The policyholder's age and family situation
healthInsurance.supplementaryContent: In addition to basic Swiss health insurance, it is advisable to take out supplementary insurance (LCA).
healthInsurance.supplementaryReason: Basic health insurance (LAMal) only covers a modest proportion of healthcare costs. Consequently, it is recommended to supplement your cover with a supplementary health contract.
healthInsurance.notMandatory: Unlike health insurance (LAMal), supplementary insurance (LCA) is not mandatory.
healthInsurance.lcaInfo: Everything you need to know about the Insurance Contract Act (LCA)
healthInsurance.crossBorderFocus: Focus on health insurance for cross-border commuters
healthInsurance.crossBorderContent: Switzerland welcomes a large number of cross-border commuters. This is why two schemes have been put in place to ensure health cover for cross-border commuters.
healthInsurance.canCrossBorderGetLamal: Can a cross-border commuter benefit from LAMal?
healthInsurance.crossBorderOptions: Cross-border commuters, whether they live in France and work in Switzerland or vice versa, are required to take out health insurance. They can choose between two solutions:
healthInsurance.cmu: CMU (using the French health insurance scheme)
healthInsurance.lamalOrCmu: LAMal or CMU? How to choose?
healthInsurance.lamalOrCmuContent: Under the LAMal Frontalier scheme, policyholders can receive care in France and Switzerland. This is not the case with CMU Frontalier, which only covers treatments in Switzerland under certain conditions.
healthInsurance.allHealthFundsContent: With the widest choice of health insurance offers, compare 2024 premiums for basic and supplementary insurance from over 30 companies in a few clicks.

carInsurance.title: Car Insurance
carInsurance.heroSubtitle: Protect yourself and your loved ones with car insurance. Find the perfect plan for your needs.
carInsurance.coverageBenefit: BENEFIT FROM COMPREHENSIVE CAR INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR YOUR PEACE OF MIND
carInsurance.introContent1: In Switzerland, mobility is an essential part of our daily lives. With nearly 6 million vehicles on our roads, the need for car insurance becomes evident.
carInsurance.introContent2: Indeed, whether you own a car, a motorcycle, or even a scooter, taking out car insurance is not only a legal obligation but, above all, an indispensable precaution to protect your financial interests and ensure your safety and that of other road users.
carInsurance.introContent3: Thanks to our Optimis car insurance guide, we will guide you through the intricacies of this complex system, explaining the various available coverages and their crucial importance in protecting your assets and your peace of mind.
carInsurance.basicCoverageIntro: When you take out car insurance in Switzerland, you have a choice of several types of coverage, each offering a different level of protection. The three main basic coverages are third-party liability, partial casco, and full casco.
carInsurance.civilLiabilityDesc: is the minimum mandatory coverage for all motor vehicles in Switzerland. It covers material damage and personal injury you might cause to third parties in an accident for which you are deemed responsible. However, it does not cover damage to your own vehicle.
carInsurance.partialCascoDesc: is an optional coverage that offers additional protection in the event of claims such as theft, natural events, glass breakage, fire, collisions with animals, marten bites, and vandalism.
carInsurance.fullCascoDesc: is the most extensive coverage you can take out. It includes all the guarantees of partial casco, but also adds protection against damage you might cause to your own vehicle in an accident for which you are responsible. This coverage is particularly recommended for new or high-value vehicles.
carInsurance.basicCoverageConclusion: I generally recommend carefully evaluating your needs and budget before choosing the coverage that best suits you. Third-party liability is essential, but partial casco and full casco offer additional protection that can prove invaluable in the event of an unforeseen incident on the road.
carInsurance.complementaryIntro: In addition to basic coverages, there is a whole range of complementary guarantees that can be added to your car insurance policy in Switzerland.
carInsurance.passengerInsuranceDesc: This guarantee covers injuries sustained by drivers and passengers in the event of an accident.
carInsurance.parkingDamageDesc: This coverage protects your vehicle against damage caused by unknown third parties when your vehicle is parked.
carInsurance.extendedGlassDesc: This option extends coverage to include damage to headlights, glass parts, and similar items.
carInsurance.mobilityAssistanceDesc: This coverage offers assistance in the event of a breakdown on the road.
carInsurance.lossOfUseDesc: This guarantee provides a replacement vehicle if your vehicle is immobilised after an accident.
carInsurance.grossNegligenceDesc: This option offers protection against recourse or reductions in benefits in the event of gross negligence on the part of the insured driver.
carInsurance.increasedValueDesc: This guarantee ensures higher compensation than the vehicle's current value in the event of theft or total loss.
carInsurance.bonusProtectionDesc: This guarantee prevents an increase in the insurance premium in the event of a claim, by maintaining the current bonus level.
carInsurance.franchiseContent1: The deductible is an essential element of any car insurance policy in Switzerland. It represents the part of the costs that the policyholder must pay in the event of a claim before the insurer begins to pay compensation.
carInsurance.franchiseContent2: A higher deductible leads to a lower insurance premium, while a lower deductible results in a higher insurance premium. It is therefore a compromise between the amount you are willing to pay in the event of a claim and the cost of your insurance premium.
carInsurance.franchiseContent3: It is important to note that each type of coverage may have its own deductible. It is therefore crucial to understand the details of your insurance policy.
carInsurance.bonusMalusContent1: In Switzerland, the bonus-malus system is a mechanism used by insurance companies to assess the risk associated with each driver and adjust the car insurance premium accordingly.
carInsurance.bonusMalusContent2: This system is based on a simple principle: drivers who have no accidents or claims are rewarded with a premium reduction, while those who have accidents see their premium increase.
carInsurance.bonusMalusContent3: The operation of the bonus-malus system is based on degrees, where each driver is assigned a certain level according to their driving history.
carInsurance.bonusMalusContent4: We advise driving carefully and respecting the Highway Code in order to maintain a good driving history and benefit from substantial premium reductions.

homeInsurance.title: Home Contents Insurance
homeInsurance.heroSubtitle: Protect your home and belongings with home contents and personal liability insurance tailored to your needs.
homeInsurance.compareDescription: Compare the best home contents insurance policies on the market.
homeInsurance.protectYourHome: PROTECT YOUR HOME AND BELONGINGS WITH SUITABLE INSURANCE
homeInsurance.watchVideo: Discover home contents insurance in video
homeInsurance.videoDescription: Our expert explains everything you need to know about home contents and personal liability insurance in Switzerland.
homeInsurance.whatIsRcMenageContent: Home contents and personal liability insurance is the perfect ally to protect both your home and your finances in case of a mishap.
homeInsurance.rcPrivateDesc: covers you if you cause damage to someone else or their property. Imagine your dog bites a passer-by or your child accidentally breaks a neighbour's bicycle: this is where personal liability insurance comes in to avoid financial hardship.
homeInsurance.menageDesc: protects everything in your flat: furniture, personal belongings, etc. In the event of fire, theft, or flood, this insurance is there for you.
homeInsurance.combinedExplanation: When these two insurance policies are combined, it creates home contents and personal liability insurance. Many companies in Switzerland offer this dual package, covering you for both damages you might cause and protecting your own belongings.
homeInsurance.whatIsCoveredIntro: Wondering what home contents and personal liability insurance covers in Switzerland? Basically, it's your home's and your wallet's best friend! Here’s what it generally covers:
homeInsurance.coverFireDesc: No need to panic if lightning strikes or a fire breaks out.
homeInsurance.coverTheftDesc: Whether it's a burglary, housebreaking, or even external theft with violence.
homeInsurance.coverNaturalDesc: Floods, storms, avalanches, rockfalls… The works!
homeInsurance.coverWaterDesc: Leaky pipes, faulty washing machines, cracked aquariums, etc.
homeInsurance.coverGlassDesc: Window panes, glass furniture, sanitary installations… It's covered!
homeInsurance.rcCoversSummary: In addition to all this, home contents and personal liability insurance covers your private civil liability if you cause bodily injury or material damage to others. In summary: your belongings inside your home and your civil liability are protected.
homeInsurance.mandatoryContent1: In Switzerland, personal liability insurance may be mandatory in certain cases, especially if you are a tenant. Landlords like to have peace of mind and often ask their tenants to provide a personal liability insurance certificate.
homeInsurance.mandatoryContent2: For tenants, personal liability insurance therefore becomes almost mandatory at the request of landlords. In other cases, it is not an obligation, but it is highly recommended to protect yourself in case of damage caused to others.
homeInsurance.mandatoryCantons: Home contents insurance is mandatory in certain cantons such as Vaud and Nidwald for fire and natural disaster coverage. In these cantons, you must subscribe with the Cantonal Fire Insurance Company.
homeInsurance.combinedInsurance: 4/ Personal Liability + Home Contents = combine them!
homeInsurance.combinedIntro: Opting for combined personal liability and home contents insurance is the ideal solution to simplify your life and protect your home. Here's why:
homeInsurance.benefit1Desc: Subscribing to two insurance policies in one is quick and efficient.
homeInsurance.benefit2Desc: No more endless administrative procedures, everything is grouped into a single contract.
homeInsurance.benefit3Desc: You are covered from A to Z with a combined insurance policy.
homeInsurance.benefit4Desc: You often benefit from a discount by opting for a combined offer.
homeInsurance.benefit5Desc: Add or remove coverage options according to your needs.
homeInsurance.benefit6Desc: The insurance protects all family members.
homeInsurance.howMuchDoesItCost: 5/ Personal Liability + Home Contents, what's the price?
homeInsurance.costContent: Prices vary depending on insurers, chosen coverage, and the value of the assets to be insured. Compare offers to find the best value for money.
homeInsurance.howToTerminate: 6/ How to cancel your current Personal Liability-Home Contents contract?
homeInsurance.terminateContent: Want to cancel your home contents and personal liability insurance in Switzerland? No problem, here's what you need to know! To cancel, you'll need a few pieces of information:
homeInsurance.terminateInfo4: A reason for cancellation (nothing too detailed)
homeInsurance.terminateDeadline: Then, send your letter of cancellation, respecting the notice period, which varies from 1 to 3 months before the end of your contract. If you forget, your contract will be automatically renewed for an additional year.
homeInsurance.optimisHelps: 7/ Want to save money? Optimis can help!
homeInsurance.optimisHelpsContent: Want to save money or improve your coverage? Optimis helps you with these steps transparently and free of charge. Compare offers and find the best home contents and personal liability insurance for you!

legalProtection.title: Legal Protection
legalProtection.heroSubtitle: Protect yourself against disputes and legal costs with appropriate legal protection insurance.
legalProtection.compareDescription: Compare the best legal protection options on the market.
legalProtection.protectYourRights: PROTECT YOUR RIGHTS WITH LEGAL PROTECTION INSURANCE
legalProtection.videoDescription: Our expert explains everything you need to know about legal protection insurance in Switzerland.
legalProtection.whatIsLegalProtection: What is legal protection insurance in Switzerland?
legalProtection.whatIsLegalProtectionContent: As a resident in Switzerland, you may find yourself facing various disputes throughout your life. For example, you might buy a defective product in a shop and be faced with a refusal of a refund.
legalProtection.whatIsLegalProtectionContent2: Legal protection insurance can prove to be a lifeline in such situations. By covering all the costs associated with legal proceedings, it offers essential peace of mind.
legalProtection.whatIsLegalProtectionContent3: Whether you initiate the legal proceedings or are sued, this insurance protects you by covering the costs incurred by the dispute.
legalProtection.typesOfProtection: What are the different types of legal protection?
legalProtection.typesContent: Legal protection insurance offers extensive cover for different types of disputes:
legalProtection.typeCirculationDesc: protects you in the event of a dispute relating to road traffic, whether you are a driver, passenger or vehicle owner.
legalProtection.typeEnterpriseDesc: covers you in the event of a dispute related to your professional activity, with a client, an employee, or for equipment purchase matters.
legalProtection.typePrivateDesc: concerns disputes under private law: consumption, employment, matrimonial law, neighbourhood, tenancy, etc.
legalProtection.typesNote: Good to know: For private and traffic legal protection, you can opt for individual or family insurance.
legalProtection.coveredItem1: Legal fees, such as lawyer's fees
legalProtection.coveredItem2: Legal advice to guide you through the process
legalProtection.coveredItem3: Support from a professional during proceedings
legalProtection.coveredItem5: Advance of bail to avoid incarceration
legalProtection.coveredItem6: Opposing party's legal costs in case of loss
legalProtection.coveredItem7: Free choice of your lawyer for legal proceedings
legalProtection.notCoveredItem1: Disputes against your own legal protection insurance
legalProtection.notCoveredItem2: Exclusions of cover for intentionally committed offences
legalProtection.guaranteesNote: Good to know: Your contract may include exclusions of cover. Before subscribing, make sure you carefully check these exclusions and any waiting period.
legalProtection.prices: What is the price of legal protection insurance?
legalProtection.pricesContent: Premiums generally vary between CHF 150 and CHF 400 per year depending on the extent of cover and the options chosen. Compare offers to find the best value for money.
legalProtection.whyNeedIt: Why do I need legal protection insurance?
legalProtection.whyReason1: Thanks to legal protection insurance, you make significant savings. The costs associated with a dispute can quickly add up. All lawyer's fees are covered.
legalProtection.whyReason2: More efficient dispute management: thanks to legal protection, you benefit from professional advice and support.
legalProtection.waitingPeriodNote: Please note: the waiting period is generally 3 months, and legal protection will not cover you for disputes that occurred previously.
legalProtection.terminationContract: Commitment and cancellation of a contract
legalProtection.terminationContent: The possibility of cancelling legal protection insurance depends on the insurers and the specific terms of each contract. As a general rule, contracts are annual and renew automatically.
legalProtection.terminationContent2: To cancel, it is generally necessary to observe a 3-month notice period before the contract's expiry date. Cancellation must be made by registered letter.
legalProtection.top10Tips: Top 10 Optimis tips for choosing your legal protection
legalProtection.tip1: Find out about different insurers using comparison websites.
legalProtection.tip2: Carefully check the guarantees and exclusions of each contract.
legalProtection.tip3: Examine the insurer's reputation and financial stability.
legalProtection.tip4: Carefully compare the prices of legal protection insurance.
legalProtection.tip5: Opt for contracts offering a free choice of lawyers.
legalProtection.tip6: Check whether you do not already benefit from legal protection in another contract.
legalProtection.tip7: Take into account waiting periods and cancellation terms.
legalProtection.tip8: Make sure that the specific disputes that concern you are included.
legalProtection.tip9: Ask for recommendations from your acquaintances or consult online reviews.
legalProtection.tip10: Accurately determine the type of contract you need.
legalProtection.coverageTypesContent: Legal protection covers different areas of law to protect you in everyday life.
legalProtection.whyNeedItContent: Legal costs can quickly run into thousands of francs. Legal protection allows you to assert your rights without financial worries.
legalProtection.howToChooseContent: Compare offers according to your specific needs and personal situation.
legalProtection.costsContent: Premiums vary according to the extent of cover and your profile. Compare to find the best value for money.

lifeInsurance.whatIsLifeInsuranceContent: Life insurance in Switzerland is a financial product that combines savings and protection. It allows you to build up capital for your retirement while protecting your loved ones in the event of death or disability.
lifeInsurance.typesContent: There are different types of life insurance in Switzerland:
lifeInsurance.type1: Pure risk life insurance: protection in case of death only
lifeInsurance.type2: Mixed life insurance: combines savings and protection
lifeInsurance.type3: Fund-linked life insurance: savings invested in funds
lifeInsurance.thirdPillarContent: The 3rd pillar is a private pension provision system in Switzerland. It complements the 1st and 2nd pillars (AVS and LPP) to ensure you a comfortable standard of living in retirement.
lifeInsurance.pillar3aDesc: Pillar 3a (tied): tax-deductible, capped amount, limited withdrawals
lifeInsurance.pillar3bDesc: Pillar 3b (flexible): no tax deduction, no contribution limit, flexible withdrawals
lifeInsurance.whoNeedsItContent: Life insurance is particularly recommended for:
lifeInsurance.needCase4: Anyone wishing to optimise their tax situation
lifeInsurance.howToChoose: How to choose your life insurance?
lifeInsurance.howToChooseContent: To choose the right life insurance, assess your protection and savings needs, compare the yields offered, and check the surrender conditions.
lifeInsurance.taxBenefitsContent: Contributions to the 3rd pillar are fully deductible from your taxable income, up to the annual limit.

lifeInsurance.maxDeductionDesc: For employees affiliated with a pension fund (2024)

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.introContent: OptimisLink Sàrl is the owner of the optimis.ch website and acts as the data controller for personal data within the meaning of the Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP). We have established this privacy policy to define our approach to processing information collected via our website. It is essential that you consult it before using our online services. The protection of your personal data is an absolute priority for us, and we are committed to guaranteeing its confidentiality and security. All data is hosted in Switzerland by Infomaniak Network SA.

about.title: About Optimis
about.missionContent: Optimis was founded with a clear mission: to simplify insurance comparison in Switzerland and to help individuals and businesses find the best offers tailored to their needs. We believe that everyone deserves easy access to optimal protection at the best price.
about.valuesContent: Independence, transparency, and customer service are at the heart of our approach. We are not tied to any insurer, which allows us to offer you objective and impartial comparisons. Our team is committed to assisting you at every step of your insurance search.
about.historyContent: Since our inception, we have helped thousands of Swiss residents save money on their insurance. Our platform compares offers from over 30 partner insurance companies, covering all types of insurance: health, car, home contents, legal protection, life, and much more.
about.teamContent: Our team of insurance experts is based in French-speaking Switzerland. We combine in-depth knowledge of the Swiss insurance market with cutting-edge technology to offer you the best possible service.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Find answers to the most common questions about our services and insurance in Switzerland.
faq.q1: How does the Optimis comparison tool work?
faq.a1: Our comparison tool analyses offers from over 30 partner insurers to present you with the best options according to your profile. Simply fill in the form, and we will instantly display the offers most suited to your needs.
faq.a2: Yes, our comparison service is 100% free and without obligation. We are remunerated by insurers when you sign up via our platform, which allows us to offer you this service free of charge.
faq.q3: Can I change my health insurance at any time?
faq.a3: Basic health insurance (LAMal) can be cancelled every year by 30th November, effective from 1st January. Supplementary insurance (LCA) has its own cancellation conditions, usually with 3 months' notice.
faq.q4: How are health insurance premiums calculated?
faq.a4: Premiums depend on several factors: your canton of residence, your age, the chosen insurance model (standard, family doctor, HMO, telemedicine) and your deductible amount.
faq.q5: What is the health insurance subsidy?
faq.a5: The subsidy is financial aid paid by the cantons to help low-income individuals pay their health insurance premiums. Eligibility conditions vary by canton.
faq.q6: What is the difference between partial comprehensive and full comprehensive insurance?
faq.a6: Partial comprehensive covers damage caused by third parties, theft, natural events, and glass breakage. Full comprehensive also includes damage you cause to your own vehicle.
faq.q7: How long does it take to receive a quote?
faq.a7: Our comparisons are instant. As soon as you have filled in the form, you will immediately receive offers matching your profile.
faq.a8: Absolutely. We comply with Swiss data protection legislation. Your information is encrypted and is never shared without your explicit consent.

rcPro.title: Professional Liability
rcPro.desc: Professional liability insurance covers damages caused to third parties in the course of your professional activities. It is mandatory for many professions in Switzerland.
rcPro.details: This insurance covers personal injury, material damage, and financial losses that you may unintentionally cause to a client or third party. The amount of cover varies depending on your sector of activity. Regulated professions (doctors, lawyers, architects, fiduciaries) are legally obliged to take out professional liability insurance.

laa.title: Accident Insurance (LAA)
laa.desc: Occupational accident insurance (LAA) is compulsory for all employers in Switzerland. It covers both occupational and non-occupational accidents for your employees.
laa.details: The LAA covers medical costs, daily allowances in the event of incapacity to work, and invalidity pensions. Employees working more than 8 hours per week are covered for both occupational and non-occupational accidents. Self-employed individuals can voluntarily take out LAA cover.

lpp.title: Occupational pension (LPP)
lpp.desc: Occupational pension (LPP) is mandatory for annual salaries of CHF 22,050 and above. It guarantees that your employees will maintain their standard of living in retirement.
lpp.details: The occupational pension (LPP) supplements OASI (1st pillar) and is an essential part of the Swiss pension system. As an employer, you must enrol your employees in a pension fund. Contributions are shared between the employer (at least 50%) and the employee. Comparing offers allows you to find the best conditions and returns.

legalProtection.title: Professional legal protection
legalProtection.desc: Professional legal protection defends you in the event of disputes related to your professional activity: contracts, employment law, commercial leases, etc.
legalProtection.details: This insurance covers legal fees, court costs, and expert appraisals in the event of a dispute. It covers contractual disputes with your clients or suppliers, conflicts with employees (employment law), tax litigation, and disputes related to your business premises.

lossOfEarnings.title: Loss of Earnings Insurance (Illness)
lossOfEarnings.desc: Loss of earnings insurance ensures salary payments in the event of incapacity to work due to illness, for you or your employees.
lossOfEarnings.details: Without this insurance, the employer is obliged to pay a salary according to the Bernese or Basel scale (from 3 weeks to 6 months, depending on length of service). Loss of earnings insurance takes over and generally pays 80% of the salary for 720 days. This is a key element for attracting and retaining talent.

multiRisk.title: Business multi-risk insurance
multiRisk.desc: Multi-risk insurance protects your premises, equipment, stock, and business against unforeseen damage (fire, water damage, theft, etc.).
multiRisk.details: This comprehensive cover includes commercial buildings, furniture and professional equipment, stock and merchandise, as well as loss of earnings in the event of a claim. It enables you to quickly resume your business after an unforeseen event.

cyber.title: Cyber Insurance
cyber.desc: Cyber insurance protects your company against digital risks such as hacking, ransomware, data leaks, and service interruptions.
cyber.details: With increasing digitalisation, cyber attacks represent a major risk for Swiss SMEs. This insurance covers data restoration costs, crisis management, notification to affected individuals (GDPR/FADP), third-party damages, and loss of earnings due to a cyber-attack.

professionalInsurancePage.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about professional insurance

faq.q1: Which insurance policies are compulsory for a company in Switzerland?
faq.a1: Mandatory insurance depends on your status and sector: LAA (accident) is mandatory for all employers, occupational pension (LPP) is mandatory from an annual salary of CHF 22,050, and professional liability insurance is mandatory for certain regulated professions (doctors, lawyers, architects, etc.).
faq.q2: Does a self-employed person have to take out the same insurance as an Sàrl?
faq.a2: No. A self-employed person with no employees is not subject to the same obligations. They can voluntarily take out accident insurance (LAA) and occupational pension (LPP). However, as soon as they employ staff, the obligations are the same as for a Ltd or plc.
faq.q3: How much does professional insurance cost in Switzerland?
faq.a3: Costs vary considerably depending on the sector, company size, and chosen coverages. Professional liability insurance can cost from CHF 300 to 5,000/year, occupational accident insurance (LAA) represents 0.5% to 3% of the total payroll, and occupational pension (LPP) between 7% and 18% of the coordinated salary.
faq.q4: How do I choose the right provider for my business insurance?
faq.a4: Compare offers from several insurers, taking into account price, scope of cover, deductibles, and customer service. Use our comparison tool to receive free, personalised offers tailored to your situation.

lpp.explainSubtitle: When you leave a job in Switzerland, your 2nd pillar doesn't disappear. It's transferred to a dormant account called vested benefits.
lpp.step1Desc: Your employer contributes to your pension fund (2nd pillar).
lpp.step2Desc: Your occupational pension (LPP) funds are transferred to a vested benefits account.
lpp.step3Desc: Without action on your part, this money can remain blocked for years.
lpp.problemTitle: Thousands of people forget their LPP
lpp.problemSubtitle: After a change in circumstances, your money may be transferred automatically... without you knowing.
lpp.problemHighlight: 💰 Your money could be dormant somewhere in Switzerland

lpp.ctaTitle: You might have forgotten occupational pension (LPP) funds
lpp.ctaSubtitle: You might have between CHF 5,000 and CHF 50,000 forgotten.
lpp.faq1Answer: Vested benefits are an account to which your occupational pension (LPP) funds (2nd pillar) are transferred when you leave a job in Switzerland without immediately starting a new one.
lpp.faq2Answer: This applies to every job change, move abroad, transition to self-employment, or period of unemployment.
lpp.faq3Question: Can I recover my occupational pension (LPP)?
lpp.faq3Answer: Yes, under certain conditions: property purchase, permanent departure from Switzerland, transition to self-employment, or retirement.
lpp.faq4Question: Where does the money go if I don't do anything?
lpp.faq4Answer: If you do not claim your funds, they are transferred to the Substitute Occupational Benefit Institution Foundation after a certain period, where they remain until your retirement.
